summary: Alfred Foucher (1865–1952) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1885 and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1928) and the University of Paris (~1907–1936).
Alfred Gell (1945–1997) studied at the London School of Economics and Political Science from around 1968 to 1971. He later held a post there from circa 1979 until 1997.

Alfred Hillebrandt (1853–1927) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Breslau (~1871–1875) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1875–1876). He served as professor at the University of Breslau (~1883–1922).

Alfred Ludwig (1832–1912) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Moriz Haupt, Anton Boller, and Friedrich Müller. He served as professor at Charles University from 1860.

Alicia Turner is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, supervised by Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and also studied under Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, committee member Christopher Winship, and teachers Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) worked in Japanology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religious Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1985–2008) and served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California (~1999–2008).

Allan Gibbard (b. 1942) is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (~1969–1977), the University of Pittsburgh (~1974–1975), and the University of Michigan (~1977).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College, attested in 2001.

Allen Wright Thrasher (b. 1946) is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1977) and studied with traditional teachers in India. He held a position at the Library of Congress from around 1985 to 2013.

Alnis Dickson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson completed an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Aloys Sprenger (1813–1893) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1832–1836). He served as principal of Delhi College (~1845–1848), Hooghly Mohsin College (1851–1854), and Aliah University (~1850–1856), later holding a post at the University of Bern (~1858–1881).

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) studied at the University of Oxford (~1962–1964) and worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the universities of Kerala, Edinburgh, Virginia, Uppsala (~1990–2005), and Arizona State University (~1990–2000).

Amalananda Ghosh (1910–1981) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1953 to 1968.

Amanda K. Goodman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. Supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., she holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Anthony Kennedy Warder and was also taught by Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Alasdair Urquhart, and Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963).

Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, and others. She has held posts at the University of St Andrews, University of York, Einstein Forum, and Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2012. In 2019, she was attested as Assistant Professor at Naropa University and online faculty at Central Michigan University.
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. She held a post as professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
